record.paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: Find a proof of maximal output p-norm multiplicativity for the two-Pauli qubit channel that does not rely on unitary equivalence to channels with negative multipliers.

evidence.quote: These channels can be described by “multipliers” in a manner similar to unital qubits channels, and when all multipliers are non-negative they seem very similar.
Problem 13. Find a proof of multiplicativity for the two-Pauli qubit channel, which does not use unitary equivalence to channels with negative multipliers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-Pauli qubit channel, the completely positive trace-preserving map on 2x2 density matrices defined, for parameters p_I, p_X, p_Y >= 0 with p_I + p_X + p_Y = 1, by

  Φ(ρ) = p_I ρ + p_X X ρ X + p_Y Y ρ Y,

where X and Y are the Pauli matrices σ_x and σ_y. Equivalently, Φ acts on the Bloch representation ρ = (I + r·σ)/2 by multiplying the Bloch components (r_x, r_y, r_z) by nonnegative multipliers (λ_x, λ_y, λ_z) with λ_x = p_I + p_X − p_Y, λ_y = p_I − p_X + p_Y, λ_z = p_I − p_X − p_Y after suitable choice of parameters; here all multipliers can be arranged so that the channel is unitarily equivalent to one with all multipliers nonnegative.

For a quantum channel Ψ and p > 1, define the maximal output p-norm

  ν_p(Ψ) := sup_ρ ||Ψ(ρ)||_p,

where ||A||_p = (Tr |A|^p)^{1/p} and the supremum is over input density matrices.

Provide a proof, valid for all p in some nontrivial range p > 1, that the maximal output p-norm is multiplicative for tensor products of the two-Pauli qubit channel with itself and with arbitrary other channels:

  ν_p(Φ ⊗ Ω) = ν_p(Φ) ν_p(Ω)   for every channel Ω,

without using a reduction by unitary equivalence to channels having one or more negative Bloch multipliers. That is, find a direct proof of multiplicativity of ν_p for the two-Pauli channel that operates within the regime of nonnegative multipliers.
artifact.status_search_result: Multiplicativity of the maximal output p-norm for the two-Pauli qubit channel is known via the unitary-equivalence reduction to channels with negative multipliers (King and collaborators), and the global maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture is now known to be false for general channels (Hastings; Hayden-Winter). However, no published proof of multiplicativity for the two-Pauli channel that avoids the negative-multiplier reduction has been located. The status of finding such an alternative proof appears unresolved in available sources.

status_evidence.title: The maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture is false
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples show the general multiplicativity conjecture fails for p>1.
status_evidence.claim: The general maximal p-norm multiplicativity conjecture is false, but this does not address the two-Pauli channel specifically.

status_evidence.title: Pauli Diagonal Channels Constant on Axes
status_evidence.snippet: Multiplicativity for a class of Pauli diagonal channels including two-Pauli is treated, often via unitary equivalence techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Existing proofs for the two-Pauli channel use the unitary-equivalence reduction the problem asks to avoid.
